core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 6782-6786): writing the given complex as the derived pushforward of some complex K, the author chooses a K-injective complex representing K, whose pushforward is again K-injective and represents the pushed forward complex.

Identify the sequence of complexes (proof lines 6787-6796): the blow-up square lemma supplies the short exact sequence of complexes of abelian groups attached to the square, with the same shape as the sequence used to define the canonical map.
Conclude (proof lines 6797-6799): since the sequence produced is exactly the one defining the canonical map, that map is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Represent the given complex as the derived pushforward of a K-injective complex.
Invoke the blow-up square lemma to obtain the exact sequence of complexes attached to the square.
Identify that sequence with the one defining the canonical map and conclude that the map is an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The helper lemma states that for a commutative square whose sheafified pushout and injectivity conditions hold, the canonical map attached to the square is an isomorphism for every complex in the essential image of the derived pushforward along epsilon (statement lines 6757-6776). The proof is short but complete: a K-injective representative is chosen so that its pushforward represents the given complex (proof lines 6782-6786), the blow-up square lemma supplies the short exact sequence of complexes attached to the square (proof lines 6787-6796), and the author observes that this is exactly the sequence defining the canonical map (proof lines 6797-6799). The non-formal content is the choice of representative and the identification of the two sequences. The claim is H1: a short reduction with two named inputs.
